mainTopic: Traits God loves and hates, the lone witness and hating a sinner, numbered aggadic lists, and teachings of רבי יוסי איש הוצל
overview: The amud opens with רבא telling רב ספרא that the praise for a sinless bachelor is meant for people like רב חנינא and רב אושעיא, who stayed pure among the זונות. The גמרא then lists three people הקדוש ברוך הוא loves and three He hates. One of the hated is a lone witness to a sexual sin, as the story of טוביה and זיגוד shows. רב rules that such a witness may hate the sinner, and רב נחמן בר יצחק says it is even a מצוה. רב אשי adds that the witness may tell his teacher only if the teacher trusts him like two witnesses. Next comes a chain of numbered lists: people whose lives are not lives, groups that hate or love each other, people no one can bear, כנען's commands to his sons, the traits of the horse, and seven who are shunned by Heaven. Teachings from רבי יוסי איש הוצל follow: do not consult astrologers, honor anyone greater than you in even one thing, and a woman waits one עונה after her days of דם טהור. The amud ends with a ברייתא listing the many names of יוסף איש הוצל, whose real name is איסי בן עקביה. A second list of names, for רבי יצחק בן טבלא, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב ספרא rejoices when the ברייתא is taught
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites the ברייתא about the praised bachelor before רבא and רב ספרא, and רב ספרא's face lights up.
steps.simpleTranslation: A teacher of ברייתות recited this ברייתא in front of רבא and רב ספרא. רב ספרא's face lit up with joy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about how two אמוראים reacted to the ברייתא from just before: הקדוש ברוך הוא praises a bachelor who lives in a city and does not sin. This line sets up רבא's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ספרא was an unmarried man living in a city who did not sin, so he believed the praise described him. His joy is the setup that רבא is about to correct.

keyTerms.meaning: A reciter who memorized and taught ברייתות in the בית מדרש
His face shone / lit up with joy

phrases.english: The tanna taught before
phrases.notes: Refers to the ברייתא about the bachelor in the city who does not sin.

phrases.english: Rava and Rav Safra,
Rav Safra's face lit up.
phrases.notes: He thought he was among those praised.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא וְרַב סָפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage. It continues the ברייתא about those praised by הקדוש ברוך הוא from the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ספרא understood the praise of the sinless city bachelor as applying to himself.

steps.title: רבא says the praise is for חכמים like רב חנינא and רב אושעיא
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב ספרא the praise is not meant for him. It is meant for רב חנינא and רב אושעיא, cobblers who worked among זונות and never looked at them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: It does not mean someone like you, Master. It means people like רב חנינא and רב אושעיא. They were shoemakers in ארץ ישראל who sat in the marketplace of the זונות and made shoes for them. The women came into their shops and looked at them, but the רבנן never lifted their eyes to look back. The women were so impressed that they would swear, 'By the lives of the holy רבנן of ארץ ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב ספרא's reading of the ברייתא. He says the praise is for people who stayed pure under extreme temptation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא sets a higher bar for 'a bachelor in a city who does not sin.' Simply not sinning in an ordinary city is not enough. The praise is for those who stayed holy while surrounded by constant temptation. Their purity was so visible that even the זונות swore by their holiness.
steps.confusionAlert: Each 'אינהו' (they) refers to a different group. The first one (מסתכלי בהו) means the women looked at the רבנן. The second one (לא מדלן עינייהו) means the רבנן did not look at the women.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Not someone like the Master,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כְּגוֹן רַב חֲנִינָא וְרַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא
phrases.english: rather, like Rav Chanina and Rav Oshaya
who were cobblers in Eretz Yisrael,
and they would sit in the marketplace of prostitutes,
and make shoes for the prostitutes,
and the women would come in to them.
They (the women) would look at them,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִינְהוּ לָא מַדְלָן עֵינַיְיהוּ לְאִיסְתַּכּוֹלֵי בְּהוּ.
phrases.english: but they (the Sages) would not raise their eyes to look at them.
And their (the women's) oath was like this:
By the lives of the holy Sages of Eretz Yisrael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב ספרא's assumption that the praise applies to him.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying the ברייתא's praise to an ordinary sinless bachelor like רב ספרא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not sinning in normal conditions does not reach the level the ברייתא praises. That level means staying pure under intense, constant temptation.

steps.title: Three people whom God loves
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא loves three people: one who does not get angry, one who does not get drunk, and one who lets go of slights.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three people הקדוש ברוך הוא loves: one who does not get angry, one who does not get drunk, and one who does not insist on his own standards, meaning he forgives and lets go when wronged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another list of 'three' in the same style as the earlier lists, this time people whom הקדוש ברוך הוא loves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three traits involve self-control: over temper, over drink, and over the urge to get even. 'מעמיד על מדותיו' means demanding payback for every wrong, so 'not' doing so describes a forgiving person.

keyTerms.meaning: Insists on his own way / demands that slights be repaid

phrases.english: Three the Holy One, Blessed be He, loves:
one who does not get angry,
and one who does not get drunk,
and one who does not insist on his measures (is forgiving).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new list of 'three' that follows the earlier lists in style.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדוש ברוך הוא loves one who is not angry, not drunk, and forgiving.

steps.title: Three people whom God hates
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא hates three people: the hypocrite, one who holds back helpful testimony, and one who testifies alone about another's ערוה sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three people הקדוש ברוך הוא hates: one who says one thing with his mouth and means another in his heart; one who knows testimony that would help his friend and does not testify for him; and one who sees his friend do a sexual sin and testifies against him by himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite list: three types of people הקדוש ברוך הוא hates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third case is the important one for what comes next. One witness cannot get anyone punished in בית דין, so his testimony accomplishes nothing except ruining the person's reputation. The next steps show this in a real story.

keyTerms.meaning: One thing in the mouth and another in the heart (hypocrisy)

phrases.english: Three the Holy One, Blessed be He, hates:
one who speaks one thing with the mouth and another in the heart,
and one who knows testimony concerning his fellow
and does not testify for him,
and one who sees a forbidden sexual matter in his fellow
and testifies against him alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite list to step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדוש ברוך הוא hates the hypocrite, the one who withholds helpful testimony, and the lone witness to an ערוה sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: The third item launches the rest of this section: the טוביה and זיגוד story and the question of whether one may hate a sinner.

steps.title: The story of טוביה and זיגוד
steps.stepSummary: טוביה sinned, and זיגוד came alone to testify before רב פפא. רב פפא had זיגוד lashed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case where טוביה sinned, and זיגוד came by himself and testified against him before רב פפא. רב פפא had זיגוד lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case that shows the third 'hated' person from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Surprisingly, the witness gets lashes, not the sinner. Since one witness cannot convict, טוביה could not be punished. זיגוד was punished for spreading a bad name, and the lashes were מכת מרדות, a rabbinic disciplinary lashing.

phrases.english: Like this case where Tuveya sinned,
and Zigud came alone
and testified against him before Rav Pappa.
He (Rav Pappa) had Zigud lashed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the third person in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That testifying alone about another's ערוה sin is condemned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רב פפא in the case of טוביה and זיגוד.

steps.title: Zigud protests the unfairness
steps.stepSummary: זיגוד objects: טוביה is the one who sinned, so why is זיגוד the one being lashed?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: טוביה sinned, and זיגוד gets lashed?!
steps.whatsHappening: זיגוד challenges רב פפא's ruling as unfair, since the sinner goes free while the witness is punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His complaint sounds reasonable: why punish the honest reporter and not the wrongdoer? This sets up רב פפא's explanation in the next step.

phrases.english: He (Zigud) said to him:
Tuveya sinned and Zigud is lashed?!
phrases.notes: This line became a popular saying for injustice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's ruling in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's decision to lash זיגוד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems backwards to punish the witness and not the sinner.

steps.title: רב פפא explains: one witness only spreads a bad name
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the תורה says one witness cannot establish guilt, so testifying alone only gives the person a bad reputation.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. As it is written, 'One witness shall not rise up against a man.' You testified against him alone, so all you did was give him a bad name.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends his ruling with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the תורה requires two witnesses, a lone witness cannot bring justice. All he achieves is הוצאת שם רע, harming someone's reputation, and that deserves punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: One witness shall not rise up against a man (דברים י״ט:ט״ו)

steps.whatToRemember: A single witness to an ערוה sin should not testify. His testimony cannot convict and only spreads a bad name, so בית דין may even punish him for it.

phrases.english: He (Rav Pappa) said to him: Yes,
as it is written: "One witness shall not rise up against a man,"
and you testified against him alone,

phrases.aramaic: שֵׁם רַע בְּעָלְמָא קָא מַפְּקַתְּ בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: you are merely giving him a bad name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, דִּכְתִיב: לֹא יָקוּם עֵד אֶחָד בְּאִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers זיגוד's objection from step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reporting a sinner is a good deed, so the witness should not be punished.
steps.terutzMaskana: A lone witness cannot convict, so his testimony is only slander and he deserves lashes.

steps.title: רב: The lone witness may hate the sinner
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a person who saw his fellow sin, though he may not testify alone, is allowed to hate him, based on the פסוק about a שונא's donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק said in the name of רב: It is permitted to hate him, as it says, 'If you see the donkey of the one who hates you lying under its load.'
steps.whatsHappening: Having said the lone witness should stay quiet, the גמרא adds that he may still hate the sinner, and brings a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of a 'שונא' whom you still must help. רב reasons that the תורה would not speak of a Jew you hate unless hating him were sometimes allowed, and the case where it is allowed is one who saw him sin. The next step checks whether the פסוק might mean a non-Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: It is permitted to hate him
The donkey of one who hates you

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said that Rav said:
It is permitted to hate him.
As it is stated: "If you see the donkey of one who hates you
lying under its load" (Exodus 23:5).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב: מוּתָּר לִשְׂנֹאתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the lone-witness case and adds a ruling about how he may feel toward the sinner.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who alone saw his fellow sin may hate him.
steps.whyThisMatters: Normally hating a fellow Jew is forbidden (לא תשנא את אחיך בלבבך). This is a notable exception.

steps.title: Which 'enemy' does the verse mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'שונא' in the פסוק means, and suggests it might be a non-Jewish enemy.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'one who hates' in this פסוק? If you say it means a non-Jew who hates you...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רב's proof by asking who the 'שונא' in the פסוק is. It raises a possibility that would weaken the proof and sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק spoke of a non-Jewish enemy, it would prove nothing about hating a fellow Jew. So the גמרא considers that reading first.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What is "one who hates"?
If you say a gentile who hates,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the פסוק that רב used as his proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the 'שונא' of the פסוק is a Jew or a non-Jew.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the enemy is a Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the non-Jew reading, citing a ברייתא that the 'שונא' in the פסוק is a Jewish enemy, not a non-Jewish one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: The 'one who hates' that they spoke of is a Jew who hates, not a non-Jew who hates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion from step 9 using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the פסוק means a Jewish enemy. That brings back the question of how a Jew could have a permitted 'enemy' at all, which points toward רב's explanation: the one he saw sinning.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge actually helps רב. By ruling out the non-Jew reading, it leaves the Jewish sinner as the only fitting 'שונא' in the פסוק.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
The "one who hates" that they spoke of
is a Jew who hates, and not a gentile who hates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion raised in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the פסוק's 'שונא' is a non-Jew.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly says the שונא is a Jew, so the non-Jew reading cannot stand.

steps.title: So the enemy in the verse must be a Jew
steps.stepSummary: Since the 'שונא' is not a non-Jew, it must be a Jewish enemy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious: the verse means a Jewish enemy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the result of the last step: the 'שונא' in the פסוק is a Jew. This sets up the next question, because hating a Jew sounds forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already ruled out the non-Jew reading. So the only option left is a Jewish 'שונא'. That raises a new problem: how can the תורה talk about a Jew whom you hate?

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish enemy (a Jew whom one hates)

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious: a Jewish enemy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion that follows from the ברייתא in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The 'שונא' in the פסוק is a Jew.

steps.title: But hating a fellow Jew is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: how can one hate a Jew when the תורה says 'Do not hate your brother in your heart'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is one allowed to hate him? Isn't it written: 'You shall not hate your brother in your heart'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that you may hate a fellow Jew. It quotes the פסוק that forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 'שונא' is a Jew, the פסוק seems to accept that you hate him. But לא תשנא forbids hating a fellow Jew. So the גמרא needs a case where hating him is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not hate your brother in your heart (ויקרא יט:יז)

phrases.english: But is it permitted to hate him?
But isn't it written: 'You shall not hate your brother in your heart'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the 'שונא' is a Jew
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה forbids hating a fellow Jew, so a פסוק cannot assume a permitted hatred of one.

steps.title: Suggestion: witnesses saw him sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the case involves witnesses who testified that he sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps it is where there are witnesses that he committed a sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries an answer: maybe the person is a proven sinner, with witnesses against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two witnesses show that he sinned, the ban on hating him would no longer apply. That would explain why the פסוק calls him a 'שונא'. The next step will test this suggestion.

phrases.english: Rather, where there are witnesses
that he committed a sin —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to the קשיא in step 12.
steps.terutzMaskana: Proposed only: hatred is allowed toward someone proven by witnesses to be a sinner. Step 14 rejects this, and step 15 gives the actual conclusion: only the person who saw the sin himself may hate the sinner.

steps.title: Then everyone would hate him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the witness case. Then everyone would hate him, so why does the פסוק single out this one person?
steps.simpleTranslation: In that case, everyone also hates him. What is different about this one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the witness idea. If the sin were publicly proven, the whole community would hate him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'your' enemy, which suggests a private hatred. A publicly proven sinner is everyone's enemy, so the suggestion does not fit the wording.

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא נָמֵי מִיסְנֵי סָנֵי לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: everyone also hates him,
what is different about this one?

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא נָמֵי מִיסְנֵי סָנֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The case of a sin proven by witnesses
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It turns a private hatred into a public one, which does not match the פסוק's 'your enemy'.

steps.title: The case: he alone saw him sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the case is where only this person saw the other do a sexual sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not a case like this one, where he himself saw him do an immoral act?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the case: only you saw him sin, so only you may hate him. This connects back to רב's ruling in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lone witness cannot testify, as we learned in step 7. But he knows the truth, so he may hate the sinner. Others did not see it, so they may not hate him.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'שונא' in the פסוק is a Jew whom you alone saw sin. You may hate him, but others may not.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not a case like this,
where he himself saw him do an immoral act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final answer after step 14 rejected the witness case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only someone who personally saw the sin may hate the sinner. This supports רב's ruling.

steps.title: It is a מצוה to hate him
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says hating such a sinner is not only allowed but a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is a מצוה to hate him, as it says: 'The fear of God is to hate evil.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק goes further than רב. He says hating this sinner is an actual מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב only said it is permitted to hate him. רב נחמן בר יצחק uses the פסוק in משלי to show that fearing God includes hating evil. So hating the sinner's evil becomes a positive duty.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה to hate him
The fear of God is to hate evil (משלי ח:יג)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
It is a מצוה to hate him,
as it is stated: 'The fear of God is to hate evil.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: מִצְוָה לִשְׂנֹאתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises רב's permission (step 8) to a מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hating a sinner whom one saw sin is a מצוה.

steps.title: May he tell his teacher so he will hate him too?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי whether one may tell his רבי about the sin so that the רבי will also hate the sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: What is the law about telling his teacher, so that he will hate him too?
steps.whatsHappening: A practical question comes up. Someone saw a sin alone. May he tell his teacher, so the teacher will hate the sinner too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the person who saw the sin may hate the sinner. The question is whether he may spread that hatred to someone he trusts, even though he cannot testify in court.

keyTerms.meaning: So that he will hate him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
What is the law about telling his teacher, so that he will hate him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a practical follow-up to the rule of hating the sinner.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a lone witness may tell his teacher about the sin, so the teacher will hate the sinner too.

steps.title: Only if the teacher trusts him like two witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers: tell him only if the teacher trusts you as much as two witnesses. Otherwise, do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If he knows that his teacher trusts him like two witnesses, he should tell him. If not, he should not tell him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a conditional answer. It depends on how much the teacher trusts the student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the teacher fully believes the student, the teacher knows the truth as if two witnesses had testified. So the teacher's hatred would be justified. If not, telling him only gives the sinner a bad name, like the problem in step 7.
steps.whatToRemember: A lone witness may share what he saw only with someone who trusts him as much as two witnesses.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִי יָדַע דִּמְהֵימַן לְרַבֵּיהּ כְּבֵי תְרֵי —
phrases.english: If he knows that he is trusted by his teacher like two witnesses —
he should tell him,
and if not — he should not tell him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי יָדַע דִּמְהֵימַן לְרַבֵּיהּ כְּבֵי תְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Tell the teacher only if the teacher trusts him as much as two witnesses.

steps.title: Three whose lives are not real lives
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three types whose lives are full of suffering: the overly compassionate, the hot-tempered, and the very sensitive. רב יוסף says he has all three traits.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: There are three whose lives are not lives: the compassionate, the hot-tempered, and the delicate. רב יוסף said: All of them are in me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new set of sayings, a series of ברייתות that list groups of three. This one lists people who suffer constantly because of their nature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each trait makes life painful. The compassionate person feels everyone's pain. The angry person is always upset. The very sensitive person is easily bothered. רב יוסף honestly admits that he has all three.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Three whose lives are not lives:
the compassionate, the hot-tempered, and the delicate.
And Rav Yosef said:
All of them are found in me.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, שְׁלֹשָׁה חַיֵּיהֶן אֵינָם חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new aggadic list, joined to the sugya by the theme of the list of threes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The compassionate, the hot-tempered, and the delicate live lives of constant suffering.

steps.title: Groups whose members hate one another
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists groups whose members hate each other: dogs, roosters, and Persian priests. Others add prostitutes and the תלמידי חכמים of בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: Three hate one another: dogs, roosters, and Persian priests. Some say: also prostitutes. Some say: also the תלמידי חכמים in בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא lists groups of three, this time groups whose members hate each other. It ties back to the theme of hatred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group competes with its own kind, for food, territory, customers, or status. The last opinion adds the scholars of בבל, who argued with each other sharply in learning.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חברין' does NOT mean 'friends' or 'study partners'. It means the Persian (Zoroastrian) priests.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה שׂוֹנְאִין זֶה אֶת זֶה, אֵלּוּ הֵן:
phrases.english: Three hate one another, and they are:
dogs, roosters, and Persian priests.
And some say: also prostitutes.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁבְּבָבֶל.
phrases.english: And some say: also Torah scholars in Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה שׂוֹנְאִין זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of aggadic lists of three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dogs, roosters, and Persian priests (some add prostitutes and Babylonian scholars) hate members of their own group.

steps.title: Three groups that love one another
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three groups whose members love each other: גרים, עבדים, and ravens.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: Three groups love one another. They are גרים, עבדים, and ravens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that is the opposite of the last list. Before, we had groups that hate each other. Now we have groups that love each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These groups stick together. גרים and עבדים are outsiders in the community, so they lean on one another for support. Ravens are known in tradition for flocking together.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Three groups love one another,
and these are they: converts, slaves, and ravens.
phrases.notes: The opposite of the list in Step 20 of groups that hate each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה אוֹהֲבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of Step 20. That step listed groups that hate each other; this one lists groups that love each other.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גרים, עבדים, and ravens love members of their own group.

steps.title: Four types of people no one can bear, plus a fifth from יש אומרים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four unbearable types: an arrogant poor man, a rich man who denies what he owes, a lecherous old man, and a פרנס who lords it over the community for no reason. The יש אומרים add a man who divorces his wife twice and takes her back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four types of people the mind cannot tolerate: a poor man who is arrogant, a rich man who lies to deny what he owes, an old man who is sexually immoral, and a community leader who acts superior to the public for no good reason. Some say: also a man who divorces his wife a first and second time and keeps taking her back.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא lists four kinds of people who are unbearable. Then a second opinion, the יש אומרים, adds one more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person behaves in a way that does not fit his situation. A poor man has nothing to be proud of. A rich man has no need to lie. An old man should be past such desires. A leader should serve the public, not look down on it. The יש אומרים add the man who keeps divorcing and remarrying because he cannot make a firm decision.

keyTerms.meaning: The mind cannot bear them (they are unbearable)
Denies (lies to avoid paying what he owes)

phrases.english: Four types the mind cannot tolerate,
and these are they: an arrogant poor man,
a rich man who denies what he owes,
a lecherous old man,
and a leader who acts superior over the community for no reason.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף הַמְגָרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ
phrases.english: And some say: also one who divorces his wife
a first and a second time, and takes her back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another short list from a ברייתא in the same series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four types are unbearable. The יש אומרים add a man who repeatedly divorces and remarries his wife.

steps.title: Why did the first opinion leave out the remarrying husband?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא קמא did not count the man who divorces and remarries among the unbearable types.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא (why didn't he include this man)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the ברייתא. It wants to know why the first opinion did not list the remarrying husband. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's behavior seems clearly annoying, so it is strange that the תנא קמא left him out. The question assumes the תנא קמא must have had a reason, and the next step gives it.

keyTerms.meaning: The first Tanna (the first opinion in the ברייתא)

phrases.english: And the first Tanna (why doesn't he include this)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the disagreement between the תנא קמא and the יש אומרים in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the תנא קמא did not list the man who divorces twice and remarries as unbearable.

steps.title: He may be forced to take her back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the husband may have no choice. Either her כתובה is too large for him to pay, or he has children with her and cannot divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes her כתובה is large (and he cannot afford to pay it). Alternatively, he has children from her and cannot divorce her (since he needs her to raise them).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 23. The תנא קמא does not blame this man, because he may be forced into taking his wife back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two reasons are given. First, divorcing her means paying her כתובה, which may cost more than he can pay. Second, if they have children together, he may need her to raise them. In either case he is not simply being indecisive, so the תנא קמא does not call him unbearable.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract, which sets the payment owed to the wife at divorce

phrases.english: Sometimes her marriage contract payment is large.
phrases.notes: He cannot afford the payment, so he takes her back.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: יֵשׁ לוֹ בָּנִים הֵימֶנָּה
phrases.english: Alternatively: he has children from her
and he cannot divorce her.

steps.whatToRemember: The יש אומרים find the remarrying husband unbearable. The תנא קמא does not, because he may be forced by money (the כתובה) or by family needs (their children).
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He may be forced to take her back, either because her כתובה is too large to pay or because he has children with her and needs her to raise them.

steps.title: The five commands כנען gave his sons
steps.stepSummary: כנען commanded his sons five things: love one another, love robbery, love lewdness, hate your masters, and do not speak the truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: כנען commanded his sons five things: Love one another, love stealing, love immoral behavior, hate your masters, and do not speak the truth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching about five instructions כנען gave his children. It ties back to the earlier list in step 21, which said עבדים love one another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כנען was cursed to be a slave (בראשית ט). So his 'commands' describe the typical behavior of slaves. The first command, 'love one another', explains why Step 21 listed עבדים as a group that loves each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Canaan, son of חם, who was cursed to be a slave

phrases.aramaic: חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים צִוָּה כְּנַעַן אֶת בָּנָיו:
phrases.english: Canaan commanded his sons five things:
Love one another,
phrases.notes: Explains why slaves love one another (Step 21).

phrases.english: love robbery,
love promiscuity,
hate your masters,
and do not speak the truth.

steps.whyThisMatters: It links back to the list in Step 21. The reason slaves love one another goes back to what their ancestor כנען taught.
steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים צִוָּה כְּנַעַן אֶת בָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the עבדים of Step 21 and explains their mutual love through כנען's command.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כנען commanded his descendants to love one another, love robbery and lewdness, hate their masters, and not speak the truth.

steps.title: Six traits of the horse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists six traits of the horse. The יש אומרים add a seventh: it may try to kill its own rider in battle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Six things are said about the horse: it loves promiscuity, it loves war, it is arrogant, it hates sleep, it eats a lot, and it excretes little. Some say it also tries to kill its owner in battle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its chain of numbered lists. This one describes the nature of the horse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The six traits are counted as six separate items: eating a lot and excreting little are two traits, not one. The יש אומרים add a seventh trait: the horse charges so recklessly into battle that it puts its own rider in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Its spirit is coarse, meaning it is arrogant

phrases.english: Six things are said about the horse:
It loves promiscuity,
and it loves war,
and its spirit is arrogant,
and it despises sleep,
and it eats a lot and excretes little.
phrases.notes: These are two separate traits, which brings the total to six.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף מְבַקֵּשׁ לַהֲרוֹג בְּעָלָיו בַּמִּלְחָמָה.
phrases.english: And some say: it also seeks to kill its owner in war.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of numbered lists, moving from the five commands of כנען to the six traits of the horse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The horse has six characteristic traits. The יש אומרים add that it endangers its own rider in battle.

steps.title: Seven people who are shunned by Heaven
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists people who are 'excommunicated by Heaven' because they neglect basic family and מצוה duties. The יש אומרים add one who skips a סעודת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Seven are shunned by Heaven: one who has no wife; one who has a wife but no children; one who has children but does not raise them to learn תורה; one who has no תפילין on his head and arm, no ציצית on his garment, and no מזוזה on his door; and one who keeps shoes off his feet. Some say: also one who does not join a group eating a meal for a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another numbered list. This one names people whom no earthly court has excommunicated, yet Heaven treats as if they were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A human court never formally bans these people. Their behavior itself puts them at a distance from Heaven. The list covers three areas: building a family, raising children in תורה, and keeping basic daily מצוות. Going without shoes is included because it is a form of self-neglect and disgrace.

keyTerms.meaning: Excommunicated (shunned) by Heaven, not by a human court
Tefillin, worn on the head and the arm
Joins a group eating a meal held for a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: If you count every phrase, the list looks longer than seven. One way to reach seven is to count תפילין on the head and on the arm as one item. That gives: no wife, no children, not raising them to תורה, תפילין, ציצית, מזוזה, and shoes. The יש אומרים then add one more.

phrases.english: Seven are shunned by Heaven, and these are they:
one who has no wife,
phrases.notes: The printed text reads 'a Jew'. The corrected reading in brackets is 'one who'.

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אִשָּׁה וְאֵין לוֹ בָּנִים,
phrases.english: and one who has a wife but has no children,
and one who has children
but does not raise them to learn Torah,
and one who has no tefillin on his head
and tefillin on his arm, and tzitzit on his garment
and a mezuzah on his doorway,
and one who keeps shoes off his feet.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף מִי שֶׁאֵין מֵיסֵב
phrases.english: And some say: also one who does not sit and eat
with a group at a meal for a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next numbered list in the series. It moves from animal nature back to human behavior.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neglecting marriage, children, Torah education, basic מצוות like תפילין, ציצית and מזוזה, or wearing shoes makes a person shunned by Heaven. The יש אומרים add skipping a סעודת מצוה.

steps.title: Do not consult astrologers
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of teachers, רבי יוסי איש הוצל teaches that one may not consult כלדיים (astrologers). He learns this from the פסוק 'תמים תהיה עם ה׳ אלהיך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי שמואל בר מרתא, who said in the name of רב, quoting רבי יוסי איש הוצל: From where do we know that one may not consult astrologers? Because the פסוק says, 'Be wholehearted with ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins, passed down through a long chain of teachers. It asks for the source of the rule against consulting astrologers and answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'תמים', wholehearted, with ה׳ means trusting Him fully. It means not trying to find out the future through the stars. The question 'מניין' (from where?) asks for a source, and the פסוק supplies it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (a request for a source)

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is a well-known source for the rule against seeking out astrology or fortune-telling. Instead, a person should rely on complete trust in ה׳.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Shmuel bar Marta said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אִישׁ הוּצָל:
phrases.english: that Rav said in the name of Rabbi Yosei of Hutzal:
From where do we know that one may not consult astrologers?
As it says: 'You shall be wholehearted with the Lord your God.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from numbered lists to a new teaching that is derived from a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not consult astrologers, because the Torah requires wholehearted trust in ה׳.

steps.title: Honor anyone greater than you, even in one area
steps.stepSummary: From the same chain of teachers: if you know someone is greater than you in even one thing, you must honor him. The source is the פסוק about דניאל and his 'רוח יתירא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that one who knows his friend is greater than him, even in just one thing, must treat him with honor? As the פסוק says: 'Because an outstanding spirit was in him, and the king planned to appoint him over the whole kingdom.'
steps.whatsHappening: The same teacher, רבי יוסי איש הוצל, gives a second 'מניין' teaching. This one is about giving honor to someone who is greater than you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the king honored דניאל and raised him up because of his outstanding spirit, his special quality. The lesson: being greater in one quality is already enough to earn honor. The person does not need to be greater in everything.

keyTerms.meaning: An outstanding, superior spirit (Aramaic, from דניאל)

steps.whatToRemember: Two practical lessons from רבי יוסי איש הוצל: do not consult astrologers, because you should be תמים with ה׳; and honor anyone who is greater than you, even in one area, as the king honored דניאל.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that one who knows about his friend

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ אֲפִילּוּ בְּדָבָר אֶחָד,
phrases.english: that he is greater than him, even in one matter,
is obligated to treat him with honor?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כׇּל קֳבֵל דִּי רוּחַ יַתִּירָא בֵּיהּ
phrases.english: As it says: 'Because an outstanding spirit was in him,'
'and the king planned to appoint him over the whole kingdom.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִין הַיּוֹדֵעַ בַּחֲבֵירוֹ שֶׁהוּא גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second 'מניין' teaching from the same chain of teachers. The word 'ומניין' (and from where) links it to the step before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must honor anyone who is greater than him in even one quality, just as the king honored דניאל for his outstanding spirit.

steps.title: After the days of pure blood, she may not be intimate right away
steps.stepSummary: The same chain of teachers adds a third teaching. A woman whose days of דם טהור are ending is forbidden to her husband right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who is sitting in her days of pure blood is forbidden to be intimate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more teaching to the series passed down in the name of רבי יוסי איש הוצל. It concerns a woman after childbirth whose days of דם טהור are ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After giving birth, a woman has a set period in which any blood she sees is טהור. Once that period ends, blood makes her a נדה. So right at the switch-over point, she must not be with her husband immediately, in case she sees blood that is now טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Pure blood': blood a woman sees during the set days after childbirth, which does not make her a נדה
'She who sits', meaning a woman who is in the middle of a set halachic period
A polite term for marital intimacy

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT saying she is forbidden during the pure days themselves. During those days she is permitted. The concern is the moment the pure days end, when any blood she sees would make her טמאה.

phrases.english: And a woman who sits in her days of pure blood
phrases.notes: This continues the chain of teachers from steps 28–29. It refers to the end of the post-birth pure period.

phrases.english: is forbidden to be intimate.
phrases.notes: Meaning right after those days end, in case she sees impure blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיּוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל דָּם טָהוֹר אֲסוּרָה לְשַׁמֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third teaching in the same series attributed to רבי יוסי איש הוצל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the days of דם טהור end, a woman may not be intimate with her husband immediately.

steps.title: How long must she wait?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long this waiting period lasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until how long?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: how long is she forbidden? It is setting up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in step 30 did not say how long the restriction lasts. This is a request for information, not a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Until how much / how long?', asking for the size or length of something

phrases.english: Until how long?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the length of the restriction stated in step 30
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long the woman must wait after the days of דם טהור end

steps.title: רב: one set time period
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that she must wait one עונה, meaning one day or one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: one עונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question: the wait is one עונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עונה is a half-day unit, either a daytime or a nighttime. By waiting that long, she can see whether blood appears at the start of her טמא period before resuming relations.

keyTerms.meaning: A set time unit: one day or one night

steps.whatToRemember: After the days of דם טהור end, a woman waits one עונה (a day or a night) before being with her husband.

phrases.english: Rav said: a set interval (one day or one night).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She waits one עונה, a day or a night.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists the many names of יוסף איש הוצל
steps.stepSummary: Because רבי יוסי איש הוצל was just quoted, a ברייתא is brought showing that he appears under many names.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: יוסף איש הוצל is the same as יוסף הבבלי, איסי בן גור אריה, איסי בן יהודה, איסי בן גמליאל, and איסי בן מהללאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of הלכה and quotes a ברייתא about who רבי יוסי איש הוצל is. The ברייתא lists many names that all refer to this same חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Different sources call the same person by different names. This ברייתא tells us they are all one person, so we do not mistake them for several different חכמים. The name 'איסי' is a short form of 'יוסף/יוסי'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He is', used here to mean 'this is the same person as'
A short form of the name יוֹסֵף / יוֹסֵי

steps.confusionAlert: These are not six different חכמים. Every name in the list refers to ONE person.

phrases.english: It was taught:
Yosef of Hutzal is
phrases.notes: The same person as the רבי יוסי איש הוצל just quoted

phrases.english: he is Yosef the Babylonian,
he is Isi ben Gur Arye,
he is Isi ben Yehuda,
he is Isi ben Gamliel,
he is Isi ben Mahalalel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא הוּא יוֹסֵף אִישׁ הוּצָל הוּא יוֹסֵף הַבַּבְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the halachic teachings to identifying the חכם who taught them
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Several names in the sources all refer to one חכם, יוסף איש הוצל.

steps.title: What is his real name?
steps.stepSummary: Out of all these names, the ברייתא asks which one is his actual name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is his name?
steps.whatsHappening: After listing many names, the ברייתא asks which one is really his. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many of the listed names may be nicknames or names taken from his city or his family. The question asks for his true personal name.

phrases.english: And what is his (real) name?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which of the listed names is the true one
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The true name of the חכם known by all these names

steps.title: His real name is איסי בן עקביה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that his real name is איסי בן עקביה.
steps.simpleTranslation: His name is איסי בן עקביה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the answer: his true name is איסי בן עקביה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every other name on the list is a nickname or an alternate title for this one person. His real name is איסי בן עקביה.

keyTerms.meaning: The true name of יוֹסֵף אִישׁ הוּצָל

steps.whatToRemember: יוסף איש הוצל, יוסף הבבלי, and the various 'איסי' names are all one person, whose real name is איסי בן עקביה.

phrases.english: His name is Isi ben Akavya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His real name is איסי בן עקביה.

steps.title: A second list: the names of רבי יצחק בן טבלא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a second example of one חכם with many names: רבי יצחק בן טבלא, also called בן חקלא and בן אלעא. The list continues past the end of this passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בן טבלא is the same as רבי יצחק בן חקלא, who is the same as רבי יצחק בן אלעא, who is the same as…
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to a second חכם who is known by several names. The list is cut off at the end of the amud and continues in the next one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works the same way as the list for יוסף איש הוצל. Different-sounding names in the sources are actually one person. The final word 'הוא' shows that another name is about to be added.

keyTerms.meaning: A חכם who is also known as בֶּן חַקְלָא and בֶּן אִלְעָא

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Tavla is
he is Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Ḥakla,

phrases.aramaic: הוּא רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אִלְעָא, הוּא
phrases.english: he is Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Ela, he is…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יצחק בן טבלא, בן חקלא, and בן אלעא are one person (the list continues).
